clue.text: Mother's scientific workplace set about making ointment

indicators.note: set about is read as turned round, so the words for mother's and the workplace are read backwards

parts.note: Ma is mother, so mother's is MA'S
a lab is a scientific workplace

explanation.surface: A mother's laboratory is busy brewing up a healing cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' turns MASLAB round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsam is a soothing resinous preparation applied to the skin, a kind of ointment.

clue.text: Designated person clearly not an uncouth fellow

definitions.meaning: someone appointed to act on another's behalf, a representative
read as two words, a gentleman, plainly no boor

explanation.surface: Someone appointed to a role is obviously no rough type.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as A GENT: a gentleman is clearly not an uncouth fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent is a representative appointed to act for someone else.

clue.text: Soldiers with time short drank outside, being held up

indicators.note: outside says the word for drank goes round the other letters

parts.note: supped means drank
OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for soldiers
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: Troops pressed for time had a drink while their progress was delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' suggests delayed, but here it means propped up; 'short' says T is the brief form of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held up in the sense of propped or borne up means being supported, not delayed.

clue.text: Singer Ethel, a fabulous creature

definitions.meaning: a mythical sea being, man above and fish below

explanation.surface: A Broadway star is praised as a wonderful being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' means of fable, not marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel Merman was the American musical-theatre singer; a merman is a legendary male sea creature.

clue.text: Weeds creating frightful ado in southern county briefly

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the shortened county name

parts.note: Wilts is the short form of Wiltshire, a county in southern England

indicators.note: frightful suggests a mess, so the letters of ado are jumbled

explanation.surface: Weeds cause a great fuss across a southern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frightful' rearranges the letters of ado; Wiltshire is a county in southern England, shortened as is usual in addresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild oats are a grass that grows as a weed among cereal crops.

clue.text: Let arch-wastrels loose — you'll create a huge financial crisis

indicators.note: let loose suggests freeing the letters to settle in a new order

explanation.surface: Set the worst spendthrifts free and you will bring about an economic disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' signals the anagram of LET ARCH-WASTRELS; 'Let' is part of the fodder, not just the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wall Street Crash of 1929 was the stock market collapse that began the Great Depression.

clue.text: See unknown character of celebrity status who gives unstinting support

definitions.note: a description of a person, standing for a noun

parts.note: lo is an old word for see or behold
Y is one of the letters used for an unknown in algebra
being on the A-list means having top celebrity status

explanation.surface: Look: a mystery figure of fame is someone who backs you all the way.
explanation.walkthrough: LO means 'see' or 'behold'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyalist is a faithful adherent who stands firmly behind a cause or ruler.

clue.text: Outstanding rugby player portrayed with halo

indicators.note: portrayed with a halo puts the ring beside the player, here in front of him

parts.note: a halo is a ring, shaped like the letter O
a wing is a rugby position on the flank

explanation.surface: A brilliant rugby player is shown with a saintly halo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' means unpaid, not excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is outstanding is still unpaid and owed.

clue.text: One hoofs around — and carpet may be ruined

indicators.note: ruined letters are wrecked and can be rebuilt in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone clattering about the floor may wreck the rug.
explanation.walkthrough: To hoof is slang for to dance; 'may be ruined' rearranges AND CARPET.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap dancer is a performer who dances in metal-tipped shoes, hoofing it about the stage.

clue.text: Time to recover, but not spiritually

parts.note: tempo is the time or speed of a piece of music
to rally is to recover strength

explanation.surface: A moment to get better, though only in body and not in soul.
explanation.walkthrough: Temporal and spiritual are paired opposites, as in the Lords Temporal and Spiritual.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporally means in worldly or secular terms, the contrast with spiritual matters.

clue.text: This writer's additional note identifies troublemakers

parts.note: this writer is the setter, I, and this writer's is I'M, I am
PS, postscript, is a note added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A writer's postscript names the mischief-makers.
explanation.definitionFit: Imps are small mischievous devils, hence little pests and rascals.

clue.text: Oil fellow's put into seats

parts.note: otto, or attar, is a fragrant oil from rose petals
man is a fellow, so fellow's is MAN'S

explanation.surface: A man's oil is poured into the chairs.
explanation.walkthrough: OTTO, like attar, is an essential oil made from roses.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottomans are low upholstered seats or footstools without backs.

clue.text: Record difficult situation that brings traffic to a standstill

definitions.text: that brings traffic to a standstill
definitions.note: a description standing for a thing, a blockage

parts.note: a log is a written record
to be in a jam is to be in a difficult situation

explanation.surface: A record-breaking tailback halts all the vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A logjam is a blockage, originally of floating timber, that stops all movement.

clue.text: Hints about depth that may be dug in garden

definitions.text: depth that may be dug in garden

indicators.note: about is read as turned around, so the word for hints is read backwards

parts.note: tips are hints or pieces of advice

explanation.surface: Gardening advice on how deep to dig.
explanation.walkthrough: A spit is a gardening term for one spade's depth of soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A spit is the depth of soil turned by one spade blade, a measure used in digging.

clue.text: One would get puffed after a violent struggle

definitions.text: One would get puffed after a violent struggle

parts.words: One would get puffed after a violent struggle
parts.note: puffed suggests a breathless fighter, but it means smoked, as a calumet was when a war ended

explanation.surface: A fighter is left out of breath after a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puffed' looks like exhausted, but means smoked: Native American peoples shared a ceremonial pipe to seal peace.
explanation.definitionFit: A peace pipe was smoked ceremonially by Native North Americans to mark the end of hostilities.

clue.text: Carer — she organised investigation

indicators.note: organised suggests the letters are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A care worker sets up an inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is systematic study, an investigation to establish facts.

clue.text: Notice a lieutenant in muddy office of navy bigwig

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement

indicators.note: in places the article and the officer inside the word for muddy

parts.note: miry means muddy, like a mire

explanation.surface: An advertisement puts a junior officer in the messy office of a senior naval figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiralty is the rank or office of an admiral, the most senior navy commander.

clue.text: Iron glove in a form of punishment

definitions.meaning: an armoured glove worn with a suit of armour
running between two lines of people who strike the offender

explanation.definitionFit: A gauntlet is a mailed glove, and running the gauntlet was a punishment of blows from two lines of men.

clue.text: Battle equipment used by Richard, war enthusiast

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A war buff named Richard makes use of military kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardware is military jargon for weapons and other fighting equipment.

clue.text: Additional supply for one who conjured up Utopia

definitions.meaning: an extra helping, as in asking for seconds
Sir Thomas ..., whose book Utopia described an ideal state

explanation.surface: Extra provisions are wanted for the creator of an ideal world.
explanation.definitionFit: More means a further amount, and Thomas More wrote Utopia in 1516.

clue.text: Gets cross in French city

definitions.meaning: ..., a city in the Loire valley

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper in a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: To anger is to make someone cross, and Angers is a city in western France.

clue.text: No seat when turned over is found to conceal a gun?

indicators.note: to conceal says the reversed words hold the article inside them
turned over says the words no and seat are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a pew is a church seat

explanation.surface: An upturned chair turns out to be hiding a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when turned over' reverses the pair before 'to conceal' puts A inside. The question mark shows a gun is only one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun is one example of a weapon, an instrument for fighting.

clue.text: Growth allows old-style educational institution to gain power

indicators.note: to gain says the college name adds the power letter after it

parts.note: a poly, polytechnic, was a British college type abolished in 1992
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: Growth lets an old college get more powerful.
explanation.walkthrough: POLY is short for polytechnic, a type of British college that became universities in 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyp is a small abnormal growth of tissue, as on a mucous membrane.

clue.text: Amount of difference when prisoner is given fresh start

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: fresh suggests something made anew, so the letters of start are rearranged

explanation.surface: A convict given a new beginning shows how much has changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges START as TRAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrast is the degree of difference between things, as between light and dark on a screen.

clue.text: Foreign food has upset us — deficient bit of beef

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned upside down, so us is read upwards
deficient says the word for the cut of beef is missing its last letter

parts.note: shin is a cut of beef from the leg

explanation.surface: Some foreign dish has made us ill, lacking any proper beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns US into SU; 'deficient' cuts the N from SHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, a foreign food to the clue's British reader.

clue.text: Maybe one's climbed a little height, getting unwell …

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for height
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A climber gets ill on reaching a modest altitude.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links into the next clue, where Bill loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hill is one example of something that is climbed, a raised piece of land.

clue.text: … which is what Bill would become if this, lacking guidance

definitions.text: which is what Bill would become if this
definitions.meaning: Bill without its first letter gives ill, the unwell of the previous clue
having no one in charge to direct

explanation.surface: Following on from feeling unwell, someone named Bill is left without direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: with its leader (first letter) gone, BILL becomes ILL, echoing 'unwell' in the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaderless means without a head or guide, hence lacking guidance.

clue.text: Send from some French district

parts.note: des is French for some
a patch is an area or district, as a police officer's patch

explanation.surface: Mail something from a particular area of France.
explanation.definitionFit: To despatch is to send off something or someone to a destination.

clue.text: This person's reversing in street that is creating obstructive situation

indicators.note: reversing says the possessive for this person is read backwards

parts.note: this person is the setter, so this person's is my
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Someone backing up in the road causes a blockage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns MY into YM.
explanation.definitionFit: A stymie, from golf, is a situation where something blocks your path, an obstruction.
